title: Tamil Nadu Politics – Evening Brief – 27 November 2026
headline: Madras High Court Refuses to Reject Nullification Plea Against CM Vijay, Deepening Legal Battles Over Perambur Disclosures

sections.big_picture:
Tamil Nadu's political landscape is currently dominated by intense judicial interventions, shifting parliamentary alliances, and high-profile criminal investigations. The Madras High Court has cleared the path for trial in petitions challenging Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's election disclosures and victory from the Perambur assembly constituency, while also barring bye-elections in three seats until pending litigation is fully resolved. Concurrently, the state administration is grappling with profound fallout from the Supreme Court's stringent orders regarding the Tirupparankundram hilltop lamp-lighting controversy, which has prompted opposition parties like the DMK to lambast the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government for allegedly compromising state rights and religious harmony.

At the national level, potential negotiations between the DMK and the BJP-led Union government regarding the upcoming amended Delimitation Bill have created significant turbulence within the state's political ecosystem. While the DMK signals pragmatic openness to support the bill on the condition that Tamil Nadu's parliamentary representation is safeguarded for a 25-year freeze, former allies such as the VCK and Left parties, alongside the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee, have vehemently criticized the move as an unacceptable U-turn. Compounding these governance challenges, the arrest of TVK legislator C. Arul Vignesh over sexual harassment allegations involving a woman IAS officer has exposed acute administrative friction, drawing fierce condemnation from opposition leaders and triggering rigorous calls for systemic accountability.

top_developments.headline: Madras High Court Clears Trial Over CM Vijay's Perambur Election Disclosures
top_developments.summary: The Madras High Court has officially refused to reject a petition seeking to nullify Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's electoral victory from the Perambur assembly constituency, effectively clearing the path for a full judicial trial. The legal challenge centers on allegations of asset concealment and discrepancies within the Chief Minister's mandatory election disclosures submitted to the Election Commission of India. In a related development, the High Court also barred bye-elections in three crucial assembly seats, including CM Vijay's former constituency of Trichy East, until all pending election petitions are definitively adjudicated....

top_developments.headline: Kallakurichi TVK MLA Arrested Over Sexual Harassment of Woman IAS Officer
top_developments.summary: Ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) legislator C. Arul Vignesh, representing the Kallakurichi Assembly constituency, was arrested by state police from his residence following a formal sexual harassment complaint filed by a woman district collector. The 36-year-old MLA was taken to a circuit house for intensive questioning under heavy police deployment surrounding his residence and office. The arrest materialized four days after the formal complaint was lodged on November 23, and 117 days after the alleged incident occurred, amid mounting pressure from the Madras High Court and the National Commission for Women. sections.government_and_administration: - **Tirupparankundram Supreme Court Fallout Triggers Severe Political Turmoil:** The Supreme Court's landmark order suspending the temple's Board of Trustees and issuing show-cause contempt notices against the Chief Secretary, DGP, and senior HR&CE Department officials has generated intense administrative friction in Tamil Nadu. BJP State President Nainar Nagenthran forcefully demanded the resignation of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, citing the apex court's strictures as definitive proof of systemic administrative failure. In response, DMK President M.K. Stalin accused the TVK government of outsourcing its core constitutional responsibilities, alleging that the administration has dangerously surrendered hard-won state rights and religious harmony built over six decades of Dravidian governance. Political analysts note that the unfolding legal saga surrounding the hilltop lamp-lighting ceremony has severely impacted executive-judicial relations within the state. ([The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/nagenthran-annamalai-welcome-sc-order-on-thirupparankundram-issue/article71751705.ece))
sections.political_parties_and_opposition: - **Delimitation Bill Redraw Sparks Alignment Between DMK and BJP While Fracturing Alliance Unity:** The DMK's pragmatic consideration to support the BJP-led Union government's amended Delimitation Bill—provided Tamil Nadu's Lok Sabha seat representation is constitutionally protected through a 25-year freeze—has realigned federal political equations. While the BJP actively courts regional parties ahead of the special parliamentary session beginning November 30, former DMK allies including the VCK, Left parties, and the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee have strongly rebuked the stance. VCK founder Thol Thirumavalavan and CPI(M) State Secretary P. Shanmugam publicly urged the DMK leadership to categorically oppose the legislation and prevent any dilution of Southern states' political leverage. TNCC President Manickam Tagore went further, accusing the DMK of executing a major political U-turn on cooperative federalism. ([The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/delimitation-redraw-brings-dmk-and-bjp-together-deepens-rift-with-congress/article71752138.ece))
sections.assembly_courts_and_policy: - **Madras High Court Advances Election Disclosures Trial for Perambur Constituency:** The legal challenges confronting Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay intensified as the Madras High Court declined to dismiss a crucial petition seeking to nullify his electoral victory in Perambur over alleged asset concealment. The bench determined that substantial triable issues exist regarding the veracity of the Chief Minister's statutory election affidavits submitted to the Election Commission. Additionally, the court ordered an indefinite stay on upcoming bye-elections across three vacant legislative seats, including Trichy East, until all related election petitions are fully adjudicated. Constitutional experts observe that these concurrent legal developments place heavy procedural scrutiny on executive compliance with electoral disclosure laws. ([ETV Bharat](https://news.google.?oc=5))
sections.district_developments: - **Tragic Electrocution Incident Occurs During Political Banner Erection in Tiruvallur:** Administrative authorities in Tiruvallur district reported a fatal electrocution accident involving two local DMK functionaries who were actively erecting celebratory banners for youth wing leader Udhayanidhi Stalin's birthday. The victims suffered severe electrical shocks when the metallic frame of the banner inadvertently came into contact with overhead high-tension power lines, resulting in instantaneous fatalities and critical injuries to a third worker. Local police registered a formal case under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, while district revenue officials initiated an independent inquiry into unauthorized banner installations. The tragic incident renewed widespread public criticism regarding the persistent flouting of safety regulations and high-court bans on illegal roadside flex-boards across Tamil Nadu districts. ([The New Indian Express](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMi-?oc=5)
sections.what_to_watch_next: Observers must closely monitor the special parliamentary session beginning November 30, during which the Union government is expected to table the amended Delimitation Bill, setting the stage for crucial floor tests and inter-party confrontations involving Tamil Nadu MPs. Legal analysts will be tracking the Madras High Court's upcoming procedural hearings regarding CM Vijay's Perambur election disclosures and the pending verdicts on assembly bye-elections. Furthermore, political circles remain alert to potential statewide protests called by Left parties and the VCK over delimitation standpoints, as well as further developments in the Kallakurichi MLA sexual harassment legal proceedings.
